comparison: Perfect agreement on empirical findings (C29-C34). Both acknowledge clear directional differences in pupil size during saccade planning with strong statistical support. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, peer reviewer also rates as SUPPORTED, noting 'clarity of the findings' and that 'a relationship between pupil size and saccade production seems clear.'

Strong disagreement on interpretation (C1, C2, C24, C27, C28, C100, C103). OpenEval rates the methodological foundation as SUPPORTED based on established literature. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly challenging 'what is at issue is the interpretation' of pupil size as effort/cost marker, stating the theoretical framework is 'too impoverished' and criticizing lack of consideration of cholinergic and dopamine systems.

Disagreement on interpretation of preference findings (C35-C45). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing converging evidence for cost-preference relationship. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the empirical relationship is clear but questioning the cost interpretation: 'Is "cost" the only conceivable hypothesis?' Also raises concerns about individual variation contradicting group trends.

Disagreement on interpretation of oculomotor conflict findings (C51-C61). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, highlighting strong evidence that costs are weighed during conflict resolution. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'clarity of the findings' for the pupil-curvature-latency relationships but questioning the cost interpretation framework and raising concerns about individual differences.

Disagreement on natural viewing experiments (C62-C64). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing robustness and generalizability.
